meanings.note: Conversational interjection.

examples.trans: Oh dear, we're in a bind.

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

meanings.en: do a favor for the speaker
meanings.note: After a te-form (会ってくれる？), warmly asks 'will you do that for us?'

examples.trans: Will you come again for me?

examples.text: 母が料理を作ってくれました。
examples.trans: My mother cooked food for me.

meanings.note: Everyday noun for time on the clock or a dedicated stretch of time.

examples.text: まだ少し時間があります。
examples.trans: There is still a little time.

examples.text: 楽しい時間をありがとう。
examples.trans: Thank you for the fun time.

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.

examples.text: 俺も金なんとか集めるからよ。もうちょっと明るくやろうや。
examples.trans: I'll scrape together some money too, so let's keep our spirits up.

examples.text: ああ。リスクもあるが、懸けてみるか、トシ。
examples.trans: Yeah. There's risk involved too, though—ready to take the gamble, Toshi?

examples.text: 強制送還の金がかかるだけで、何の見せしめにもならないだろ？
examples.trans: Deporting them just costs money and doesn't serve as an example to anyone, right?

meanings.note: Means 'spot' in 近いところ, and 'as far as today goes' in 今日のところは.

examples.text: 静かなところが好きです。
今のところは順調です。
examples.trans: For the moment, things are going smoothly.

meanings.en: nothing more than (after past verb); up to
meanings.note: After a plain verb + です (出店したまでです), modestly states 'we simply did that and nothing more'.

examples.text: 念のため聞いたまでです。
examples.trans: I merely asked just in case.

meanings.note: Irregular verb: くる -> きます -> きました.
Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Interrogative pronoun for place.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Opposite of 表 (public surface); 裏の世界 means 'the underworld / hidden world'.

examples.text: 裏の世界を見せてやろうか。
examples.trans: Shall I show you the hidden world?
Write on the back of the paper.

meanings.en: open a store; bring out; hand in
meanings.note: 店を出す means opening a branch; 出しやがって attaches tough-guy disdainful やがる.

examples.text: 駅前に新しい店を出します。
examples.trans: We open a new branch in front of the station.

examples.text: 書類を出してください。

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Signals recognizing someone ('Oh, Toshi!') or letting out a feeling ('Man, I'm hungry').
In casual speech, それ plus は often fuses into そりゃ ('well, as for that / of course').
Limits the preceding noun or phrase to that item alone.

examples.text: これだけお願いします。

meanings.note: Adverbial noun used for strong certainty.

examples.text: 明日は絶対に来てください。

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Read なん before だ/です/の, and なに before が/を or alone.

examples.text: 何を買いにきましたか。
examples.trans: What did you come to buy?

meanings.en: exist; be available; remain in place
meanings.note: Used for inanimate things and abstract concepts; after て-form (書いてある, 置いてある) describes a resulting state left in place.

examples.text: 名前が書いてあります。

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Ichidan verb: blunt imperative 見ろ ('look!') is rough command speech.
Attaches to a past-stem verb form to set up a condition ('if a fire starts').

examples.text: 火事になったら大変です。
examples.trans: If a fire breaks out, it will be terrible.

examples.text: 家に帰ったら電話します。
examples.trans: I will call when I get home.

examples.text: もし見つけたら、取引停止にしてもらって結構です。
examples.trans: If you ever catch us doing that, feel free to halt all business with us.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: After なくて (隠さなくて結構です), politely says 'there is no need to'.

examples.text: 明日は来なくて結構です。
examples.trans: You do not need to come tomorrow.

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Mental readiness to face something difficult or risky.

examples.text: この世界に入る覚悟はあるのか？
examples.trans: Are you prepared to enter this world?

meanings.note: Noun; takes する.

examples.text: みんなから期待されている。
examples.trans: Everyone has high expectations for me.

meanings.note: Standalone pronoun ('this'), unlike この which requires a noun.

examples.text: 時代が変わりましたね。

meanings.note: Casual, slightly rough noun for a person or thing.

examples.text: あいつは面白いやつだ。

meanings.note: Blunt or rowdy second-person pronoun used with subordinates, rivals, or close crew.

examples.trans: I leave it to you guys.

meanings.note: Asks about condition, outcome (どうだった), or what happened (どうしましたか).

examples.text: 女性の性の解放っていうんですかね。そういうのに憧れて、私もやってみようかなって。

examples.trans: Just like you promised, let them go soon.

examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Second-person pronoun used by superiors, in songs/books, or between close friends.

examples.text: 君の意見はどうですか。
君ならきっとできるよ。
もちろん望むところです。
examples.trans: Of course—I wouldn't have it any other way.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。

examples.trans: Are you prepared to enter this world?

meanings.note: Reassures that rules or steps are followed properly.

examples.text: ちゃんと確認しました。
ちゃんと並んでいます。

meanings.note: First-person pronoun commonly used by men and boys in friendly or polite everyday settings.

examples.text: 僕もコーヒーをください。

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
